notes: Verified against the listing and Hex-Rays 0x31f410: the body is LDR R0,[R0,#0x68]; BX LR, and (DWORD*)this + 26 is +0x68, so it returns the word at +0x68. What that word IS depends on the original string layout and is an OPEN QUESTION recorded in TRACK-B-STATUS.md: the sibling getXML (0x31f418) returns this+0x70 and setValue/loadXML treat +0x54 as a std::string, and in the original STLport-like layout the data pointer of a string at +0x54 sits at +0x54+0x14 = +0x68, which would make +0x68 a char* to the root group name rather than an int id. The port keeps an int there. Either way the port reads the same word the binary reads, so the word offset is right; the type is the open part.

Verified against Hex-Rays 0x31f418: the original body is a single instruction, `return this + 112`, the ADDRESS of the xml-name member at +0x70 cast to char* - the address of the std::string object, not its text. The mangled symbol encodes no return type, so this signature is symbol-compatible; returning `const std::string&` is a deliberate, documented port deviation (a pointer into a std::string is not a usable interface), and it is the only deviation on this row. The layout the old note said was missing now exists in the class itself (CTweakable.hpp, +0x00..+0x7b, xmlName at +0x70). A non-virtual getXMLString() gives the LC_API_STRCMP callers the C-string form without introducing a symbol.
